content.key_idea: A single Event Mux aggregates doorbell, credit, and dequeue events to keep small per-QP scheduling state in QPC, letting the scheduler pick among tens of thousands of QPs without caching WQEs.
content.reading_order: Top to bottom: WQEs move from the host's Data Buffer into SQ1, whose doorbell, plus Congestion Control's credit signal, drive Event Mux and the QPC/Schedule Policy/Schedule Queue loop below.

summary: Figure 6 details SRNIC's cache-free SQ scheduler, a subsystem of the RNIC's transport layer. On the host, a Data Buffer feeds work queue elements (WQEs) into send queues SQ1 through SQ4; when SQ1 receives new WQEs it rings a doorbell to the RNIC's Event Mux (EMUX). EMUX also receives credit updates from Congestion Control and dequeue events from the Schedule Queue, and on any of these events it updates each queue pair's scheduling state (active, credit, ready) stored in QPC without caching the actual WQEs. A Schedule Policy consults QPC to pick queue pairs that are both active and credited, enqueuing them into the Schedule Queue, which in turn feeds back into EMUX. The whole scheduler subsystem is drawn nested inside the RNIC's DMA Engine, below the host's send queues.
